cif_read — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.cif_read(cif, name=None, default_b=0.5) (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.cif_read(cif, name=None, default_b=0.5); from the registry, opsdrive.get("cif_read"))

Usage

Reads a CIF (the standard format for crystal structures) and returns a "phase" expanded to all atoms in the unit cell.

cif is a file path or the CIF text (a string; treated as text if it contains data_ or _cell_length_a). What is read: _cell_length_a/b/c, _cell_angle_alpha/beta/gamma, the symmetry-operation loop (_space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz; identity only if absent), the atom loop (_atom_site_fract_x/y/z, _atom_site_type_symbol (if absent, the element symbol at the start of the label), _atom_site_occupancy (default 1), _atom_site_U_iso_or_equiv or _atom_site_B_iso_or_equiv (if absent, default_b [Å²])). Parenthesised numeric uncertainties (4.76050(5)) are dropped. Symmetry operations are read with a small home-made parser, without eval.

Return value (dict, phase): name, cell (a, b, c [Å], α, β, γ [deg]), volume [Å³], atoms (list of atoms after expansion:

type, xyz, occ, B), cell_mass [g/mol], density [g/cm³], notes (ions substituted by neutral atoms etc.), source (DOI and COD number if present). Input to powder_reflections and phase_dictionary.

Raises ValueError: lattice constants missing / not numeric, symmetry operations unreadable, no atoms, element without scattering factors.
